entries.mutant: L197 string 'the run continued a lineage with spend no evidence accounts for (' emptied
entries.group: Leading subject clause of the operator note for a run that continued a lineage with unaccounted spend accepted by name; the pinned/documented carrier ('accepted by name') and the identifying tail (the field name continues.accepted_unaccounted, the count, 'the lineage's total is not known') survive in the kept literal, and the only reader plus the documented contract assert 'accepted by name'.
entries.grounds: verify.py L195-L199 appends ONE note, inside `if accepted:` which is inside `if s is not None:` (L187), i.e. only for a run whose journal reconstructs and whose settings bind and whose `rec['continues']['accepted_unaccounted']` is non-empty (run.py L548 writes that field on `aisef run --parent --accept-unaccounted` over spend the evidence reads as sent-and-unanswered, ADR-8). The note is two adjacent string literals concatenated; the mutant empties the FIRST, giving `f"{len(accepted)} listed in continues.accepted_unaccounted), accepted by name: its ceilings were enforced against the known part, and the lineage's total is not known"` (confirmed by mutant_view and by building the module: grep of the mutant shows exactly that text). The second literal — carrying 'accepted by name', 'its ceilings were enforced against the known part', 'the lineage's total is not known' — is UNCHANGED. The mutant does not change whether a note is appended (notes.append still fires) nor the list length, only the text of this one note; the verdict is unaffected (the note is never a problem). The note reaches the operator only through cli._print (cli.py L56-L57) which json.dumps the whole document with sort_keys (dict keys only; the note string and the notes list order print verbatim) and returns exit code from v['verdict'] alone (L59); nothing in the pipeline parses the note. MEASUREMENT: built a COPY of the tree with the mutated module and ran the target's registered kill files that exercise this branch, with PATH stripped of both dirs holding an opencode binary and HOME/TMPDIR/XDG under the copy: test_v21_x_lineage_proof (the only file that asserts on v['notes'] for this note) 55 tests OK; test_v21_continue_usage 10 OK; test_v21_continue_integrity OK. Baseline (unmutated tree) single method OK. No kill file fails on the mutant, so the campaign's SURVIVED is explained with no appeal to environment or order: the sole note reader (x_lineage_proof L1040) asserts `any('accepted by name' in n for n in v['notes'])`, which the mutant keeps. What is lost is the subject-framing 'the run continued a lineage with spend no evidence accounts for' and the opening '(' of the parenthetical count; the remaining tail still states the money-safety condition (unaccounted spend accepted by name, ceilings against the known part, total unknown) and names the field, so an operator is not misled into anything false — the same pattern held AUDITED for the sibling note mutant [index 132] and the problem mutant [index 106] in this batch, where identifying content survives in the kept text and no document/consumer parses the whole string. Held AUDITED on those carriers; it is a relatively aggressive clause removal, so an optional consistency test is noted below (a choice, not a gap).
consumers_checked: aisef2/app/verify.py L195-L199: sole producer of this note; L222-L223 the returned document (the 'notes' field)

aisef2/app/cli.py L56-L57 (_print = json.dumps(doc, indent=1, sort_keys=True, default=str)) and L58-L59 (exit 0 on VERIFIED else 1): the operator sees the note as a JSON string, sort_keys orders dict keys only, the note text and the notes list order are printed as given, nothing is parsed

tests/v2/test_v21_x_lineage_proof.py L1014-L1040 (NoFlagOpensAPaidSession.test_a_request_in_flight_is_still_refused_without_the_flag_and_accepted_by_name_with_it): the ONLY reader of this note; L1038-L1039 assert (verdict, problems) == ('VERIFIED', []), L1040 asserts any('accepted by name' in n for n in v['notes']) — 'accepted by name' is in the UNMUTATED second literal, so it passes (ran: 55 tests OK on the mutant). Its L1018 `assertIn('no evidence accounts for', text)` reads text = refused_at_the_claim(...) which returns str(the RunRefused) (helper L755-L770), i.e. run.py L545's refusal, a different producer — not this note
tests/v2/test_v21_continue_usage.py L167-L170: calls verify() and asserts (v['verdict'], v.get('problems')) == ('VERIFIED', []); does not read v['notes'] (ran: 10 tests OK on the mutant)
tests/v2/test_v21_continue_integrity.py L287 and L302: assert on rec['continues']['accepted_unaccounted'] (the RECORD's field written by run.py L548), never on the verify note (ran on the mutant: OK)

git grep 'continued a lineage' over aisef2/validation/tests/docs: verify.py L197 only — no other reader anywhere; git grep 'accepted by name': verify.py L198 (kept), aisef2/app/client.py L87 and aisef2/app/lineage.py L89 (code comments), test_v21_x_lineage_proof.py L1040 (kept), docs; git grep 'no evidence accounts for': run.py L545 (RunRefused), cli.py L47 (--accept-unaccounted help), verify.py L197, test docstrings (A13 L8) and the CLI help pin (test_v21_kills_cli.py L63), x_lineage_proof L1018 (reads the refusal, not this note) — no reader reads THIS note for that phrase

validation/qualification/v21_q5_compare.py L129 and validation/qualification/c2_orchestration_repair.py L242/L305 compare a 'notes' field between a reference and a candidate observation, but those are q5 / orchestration-repair observation notes, not verify's lineage note; and both sides run the same code, so a text change there would be identical on both

validation/v21/cli_integration/e2e_guest.py L473 and L790 record vj['notes'], but only for a run WITH a manifest (the anchor-match note, per the batch's index 132 audit); no e2e scenario continues a lineage with accepted_unaccounted, so this note never appears in the e2e evidence

docs/v2.1/USAGE-2.1.md L821-L822 (R4/8.5) and docs/v2/V2.1-BACKLOG.md V21-79: the documented note contract is the phrase \"accepted by name\" (kept by the mutant); neither quotes or promises the leading clause
exceptions_checked: a reader matching the whole note, or its start ('the run continued ...'), by exact string / regex / startswith: git grep over aisef2, validation, tests, docs finds none; the only assertions on this note are the substring 'accepted by name' (x_lineage_proof L1040), which the mutant keeps

the mutant changing whether/how many notes are appended rather than the text: no — notes.append still fires, the list length is unchanged; the only length-of-notes assertions in the suite are for runs that do not enter this branch (no accepted_unaccounted), so they are untouched

the operator being misled into a false reading: the surviving tail still says 'accepted by name', 'its ceilings were enforced against the known part' and 'the lineage's total is not known', and references continues.accepted_unaccounted; nothing false is stated, only the subject-framing and the opening '(' are lost (the count prints without its '(')

the unbalanced '(' reaching another note or field: notes are separate list elements and cli prints each as its own JSON string; no join concatenates notes, so the dangling '(' cannot swallow following text

round 3 paths: the note is reached only after the journal reconstructs and the six projections admit it and s is not None; after a projection refusal or an unreadable journal, events == [] and either s is None (no spec) or the spend check diverges before L195, so the branch is not entered; the mutant's effect is confined to its own literal on the one path that produces the note

the kill-file measurement itself: baseline single method OK; on the mutant test_v21_x_lineage_proof 55 OK, test_v21_continue_usage 10 OK, test_v21_continue_integrity OK — no kill file fails, so SURVIVED needs no environment/order explanation
